transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I’m constantly losing the tools and paperwork I need at work, and it’s starting to cause real problems on the line. I work at a meat processing plant, and misplacing things like my knives or the inventory logs is slowing down production and getting me into trouble.

Have you had problems with losing things, staying organized, or paying attention since you were a child or teenager, or did this mainly start after a recent stressor or life change? If there was a stressor, what was it?

I've actually struggled with this since childhood; my primary school teachers always commented on my report cards that I daydreamed a lot, lost worksheets, and forgot instructions. However, it became much more overwhelming recently when I transitioned to a fast-paced, full-time role at the meat plant, started training new staff, and tried to juggle dense certification courses on top of rotating shifts.

Do these attention and organization problems happen even when you’re feeling calm, or do they mainly get worse during periods of strong worry, nervousness, or physical anxiety symptoms like a racing heart? Have you been dealing with excessive anxiety about many areas of life for at least several months?

I don't really experience constant nervousness or excessive anxiety about different areas of my life, and these attention struggles happen all the time, even when I am feeling completely calm. I definitely get stressed and frustrated as a result of losing things and making mistakes, but I don't have physical symptoms like a racing heart.

Besides the inattention and losing things, have you also had lifelong problems with restlessness, fidgeting, interrupting people, or acting before thinking? Or have your difficulties mostly been with attention and organization?

No, I don't really struggle with physical restlessness, fidgeting, or acting impulsively. My difficulties have almost entirely been with attention, focus, and organization, like daydreaming and losing track of my things. That has really been the pattern for me ever since I was a kid.

final_diagnosis.reason: Lifelong pattern of attention and organization difficulties beginning in childhood, with persistent distractibility, losing necessary items, forgetting instructions, and occupational impairment. Symptoms occur even when calm and are not better explained by generalized anxiety. Hyperactive/impulsive symptoms are denied, supporting predominantly inattentive ADHD.
